title.narrative: Macrofinancial support to Ukraine through the World Bank's Ukraine Facility FREE

description.narrative:
The Russian invasion has created great uncertainty about the finances of the Ukrainian state and has specifically resulted in a large gap in the treasury, while Ukraine de facto has no access to the international capital markets to finance public spending and welfare services in the country.
Based on the economic situation in Ukraine, the World Bank, under the auspices of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), has established FREE, Financing of Recovery from Economic Emergency, as a new emergency, supplementary loan facility for Ukraine under the bank's country program for Ukraine. The Danish contribution of DKK 150 million is financed by tying up the otherwise untied funds that Denmark provides to the World Bank's development department IDA. The World Bank has agreed to this. Denmark has chosen the grant modality in order to be able to help Ukraine as quickly as possible.
The new facility FREE will provide general budget support to Ukraine and will focus on keeping the public sector in Ukraine running through the crisis, including, among other things, by financing salary payments to healthcare professionals, school teachers and public employees as well as benefits for particularly vulnerable groups, pension funds and contributions to students.
